stories.headline: LIV Golf Secures Unnamed Investor To Survive Saudi Funding Loss
body: Golf league LIV approved a mystery backer's term sheet to replace the Saudi Public Investment Fund, which recently withdrew its financial support.
London-based private equity firm BC Partners is reportedly considering a loan to keep the golf tour operating through the 2030 season.
The revamped league will feature 10 global events and make players majority owners, allowing them to freely compete on rival golf tours.

stories.headline: Betting Operator Super Group Posts Record $684M Revenue And $123M Profit Following US Exit
body: Super Group, the parent company of global sportsbook Betway, achieved a $123M profit compared to last year's $3M loss, validating its US market exit.
Total revenue jumped 18% to $684M, fueled by steady international casino play and a massive spike in sports wagers during the FIFA World Cup.
Monthly active players grew 13% to 6.2M, giving the business a highly profitable user base to monetize across international sports and casino platforms.

stories.headline: Corporate Ad Spending On Digital Creators Will Reach $21B By 2026
body: Top YouTube star MrBeast recently hit 500M subscribers and is expanding his online channel into a massive company selling toys and financial apps.
To capture surging ad dollars, internet personalities are adopting corporate structures by hiring chief executives and securing institutional investor funding.
Meanwhile, traditional media companies like Hearst and Business Insider are replacing key executives and restructuring operations to survive this industry shift.

stories.headline: Callaway Golf Raises Full-Year Outlook Following Strong Second-Quarter Sales
body: The golf equipment maker reported second-quarter revenue of $612.2M, beating expectations and prompting a raised full-year sales forecast of over $2B.
Growth was driven by a 15% jump in golf ball revenues, helping the brand capture a record 23% share of the US market.
To boost profitability, the business will close four underperforming retail stores and reward investors through an ongoing $200M stock buyback program.

stories.headline: Disney Sells Out Super Bowl Ad Space In Record Time
body: The media giant secured deals with 58 brands, marking the earliest a network has ever sold all ad spots for the big game.
While Disney hid exact prices, industry experts estimate a 30-second commercial cost between $8.5M and $9M due to soaring advertiser demand.
This early sellout guarantees massive revenue, with Disney expected to beat competitor NBC’s previous $920M sales record for the highly viewed sporting event.

stories.headline: Atlanta Braves Report Drop In Media Revenue Following TV Network Bankruptcy
body: The Braves, the only publicly traded baseball team, saw second-quarter media earnings fall to $72.85M, representing a 10% drop from last year.
This decline follows the bankruptcy of their former broadcaster, regional channel FanDuel Sports Network, which forced the team to launch its own network.
The team blames the drop on payment delays from their new network, highlighting broader industry struggles to replace lost cable television revenue.

stories.headline: Brookfield Takes Full Control Of Oaktree And Italian Soccer Club Inter Milan
body: Canadian investment giant Brookfield bought the remaining 26% of US fund Oaktree, reportedly for $3B, valuing Oaktree at about $11.5B.
Oaktree has owned Inter Milan since May 2024, seizing the club after previous Chinese owners Suning failed to repay a loan.
Reports suggest Brookfield and Oaktree may now sell Inter, the reigning Serie A champions, whose finances have recovered sharply since the pandemic.

stories.headline: FIFA President Retains Leadership Support After Failed Private Investment Plan
body: FIFA President Gianni Infantino faced massive backlash after attempting to sell stakes in global soccer tournaments to private investors.
Despite the failed proposal, top executives at the soccer governing body backed his continued leadership during a recent crisis meeting.
The president still faces intense pressure to resign from regional soccer organizations ahead of a leadership election next March.

editions.title: Middle East Conflict Crushes F1 Revenue By 38%

stories.headline: F1 Revenue Falls 38% After Middle East Conflict Postpones Races
body: Liberty Media, the US owner of F1, saw Q2 racing revenue fall to $764M from $1.22B a year earlier.
Only five races were held versus nine last year, after Bahrain and Saudi Arabia were postponed over regional conflict.
MotoGP, which Liberty bought last July for $3.1B, posted a slight 2% revenue dip to $170M.

stories.headline: Sports Betting Firm DraftKings Reports a Revenue Dip to $1.4B Despite Surging Customer Activity
body: Sports betting company DraftKings saw second-quarter revenue fall 5% to $1.4B, even though total customer wagers jumped 15% to $13.1B.
The revenue drop happened because bettors won more games and the company spent heavily on promotions for its new sports prediction platform.
Despite the shortfall, the company maintained its annual profit targets of up to $900M, banking on growing user engagement before football season.

stories.headline: Measurement Giant Nielsen Acquires Ad Safety Firm DoubleVerify For $2.15B
body: Nielsen, a major TV audience measurement company, is paying cash for DoubleVerify, a firm that checks if digital ads are actually seen.
The acquisition expands Nielsen's business beyond traditional television ratings by adding tools that ensure online ads appear on safe, legitimate websites.
DoubleVerify recently reported $193.8M in quarterly revenue, proving its steady financial value as a platform for tracking digital media effectiveness.

stories.headline: UK Soccer Club Arsenal and Airline Emirates Sign £70M Sponsorship Extension
body: Airline giant Emirates will pay UK soccer team Arsenal £70M annually until 2033 to sponsor its stadium, jerseys, and training facilities.
This deal raises the yearly payout by £20M, making it the most lucrative sponsorship in the league following Arsenal's recent championship victory.
The partnership began in 2006 and remains the longest-running jersey sponsorship in English soccer, offering the airline unmatched global brand visibility.

stories.headline: Media Giant Fox Rejects Early Talks For NFL Broadcast Rights
body: Broadcast partner Fox Corp. told investors it will avoid new NFL contract talks until a formal opt-out clause kicks in during 2030.
The popular sports league had hoped to secure new, updated television agreements several years ahead of schedule.
While Fox enjoys massive TV ratings, the network recently criticized the NFL for moving more games to paid streaming platforms.

stories.headline: Portland Trail Blazers Secure $101.6M County Approval For Arena Renovation
body: Local government Multnomah County approved $101.6M to upgrade the aging Moda Center arena, aiming to keep the NBA's Portland Trail Blazers from relocating.
The basketball team is requesting $573M total from local and state governments to finance the renovation and sign a new long-term lease.
This preliminary approval moves the deal forward as the city of Portland prepares to vote on its $120M share amid tense contract negotiations.

stories.headline: LIV Golf Sets Up Single-Event Company As It Restructures After Saudi Exit
body: Law firm Gibson Dunn incorporated LIV Golf Bedminster LLC on July 15, weeks before the league's tournament at Trump National Bedminster.
Housing each event in its own company can shield assets from creditors, useful as LIV fights lawsuits in the US and UK.
Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the league's sole backer, cut funding this year; LIV now cites an unnamed new investor.

stories.headline: European Football Body UEFA Continues FIFA Boycott Over World Cup Sale Dispute
body: UEFA, European football's governing body, refuses to play in global tournaments until FIFA guarantees it will never again try to sell World Cup shares.
FIFA president Gianni Infantino is facing growing calls to resign and has lost endorsements from multiple European nations ahead of the 2027 election.
The ongoing protest threatens the participation of European teams in upcoming major international tournaments, starting with the September U-20 Women's World Cup.

stories.headline: Tom Brady Rapidly Expands Co-Owned Trading Card Chain CardVault
body: The retired NFL star owns half of CardVault, a physical retail chain planning to open 100 locations across major US malls and stadiums.
The expansion targets a massive market boom, as the trading card industry skyrocketed from $10B to $50B after the pandemic.
Backed by Brady's star power and connections to sports merchandise giant Fanatics, the retailer projects a 400% revenue jump next year.

stories.headline: KKR Reveals $8.8B Value Of Newly Acquired Sports Investment Firm Arctos
body: Investment giant KKR recently bought Arctos, a firm holding $8.8B in minority stakes across pro teams like the Golden State Warriors.
Arctos’ two main sports funds have generated a strong 22% net return for their investors by backing major sports franchises.
Building on this success, the firm is raising a third sports fund and expanding into new industries like real estate.

stories.headline: Under Armour Lowers Revenue Outlook And Cuts Product Offerings By 25 Percent
body: The sportswear brand faces weak demand in the US and Asia, expecting its full-year revenues to decline by high single digits.
Founder and CEO Kevin Plank plans to cut product options by 25% to sell fewer items at higher, full-retail prices.
Despite recent sports marketing wins, quarterly sales fell 3% to $1.1B, dropping the company's total profit to just $1M.

stories.headline: PENN Entertainment Funds Online Expansion With Record $1.5B Casino Revenue
body: PENN, a major US casino operator, generated a record $1.5B from physical casinos which helps fund its expanding online gambling platforms.
The online betting division lost $9.5M but made $349M in sales, showing strong growth after ending an expensive partnership with sports network ESPN.
Linking profitable physical casinos with online apps allows the company to attract younger players while keeping marketing costs strictly under control.

stories.headline: WNBA Viewership Increases 15% Due To Expanded TV Coverage And Star Players
body: The women's basketball league is averaging 756K viewers per game, up 15% from last year because of more network television availability.
Standout rookie player Caitlin Clark has driven massive ratings, featuring in all ten of the league's largest TV audiences since 2000.
A recent game drew 2.52M viewers, helping the league secure nine of the top 22 overall sports broadcasts in a single week.

stories.headline: FIFA Condemns Coordinated Effort To Remove President Gianni Infantino
body: UEFA, European soccer's governing body, threatened a World Cup boycott over FIFA's canceled plan to sell tournament rights to private investors.
Tensions escalated after reports revealed UEFA previously paid a six-figure sum to Infantino’s alleged former partner, an accusation he strongly denies.
While European and North American soccer organizations demand new leadership, African and several Latin American federations continue to back the current president.

stories.headline: Oregon County Approves $101.6M To Fund Portland Trail Blazers Arena Renovations
body: The $101.6M agreement is part of a larger $600M public project to renovate the aging Moda Center.
Officials hope this framework convinces the NBA and team owner Tom Dundon to keep the basketball franchise in Portland.
Despite the vote, the county has not identified its funding source, and Dundon refuses to pay for any upgrades himself.

stories.headline: Saudi Wealth Fund Chief And Potential Investor Meet With Trump At LIV Golf Event
body: Yasir Al-Rumayyan, head of Saudi Arabia's wealth fund, was seen with Donald Trump at a LIV Golf tournament.
The Saudi fund recently pulled its funding after spending billions, forcing the golf league to seek new financial backers.
Ted Goldthorpe, head of investment firm BC Partners, was also present and is reportedly considering funding the league.

stories.headline: DraftKings CEO Warns Prediction Markets Pit Casual Bettors Against Wall Street Pros
body: Jason Robins, chief of sports betting giant DraftKings, says rival startups wrongly advertise their platforms as simple peer-to-peer betting spaces.
He notes that over 90% of trading volume actually comes from professional financial firms, leaving everyday users at a massive disadvantage.
Robins also criticized competitors for giving financial perks to these professional traders instead of rewarding the casual customers who typically lose money.
